title: Earth at Night
subtitle: City lights, as seen from orbit

source.agency: NASA Earth Observatory · VIIRS Black Marble

facts: The Black Marble is a composite of cloud-free night images from the VIIRS instrument on the Suomi NPP satellite. What you are hearing is not a photograph of cities — it is a map of how much light reaches orbit from the ground.
journeyIntro: This is our planet with the sun taken away. Every bright speck is somebody's street. Move across it and the sound will tell you where people are and where the dark is.

hotspots.name: The American east coast
hotspots.text: The east coast of North America, drawn in light. The dense chain from Boston to Washington is one of the brightest continuous lines on the planet.

hotspots.name: Europe
hotspots.text: Western Europe, almost solid with light. The dark gaps are mountains and sea — the Alps, the North Sea, the Bay of Biscay.

hotspots.name: The Nile
hotspots.text: A thin bright thread through the dark: the Nile, and the farms along it. Everything on either side is desert, and in this picture the desert is genuinely black.

hotspots.name: India
hotspots.text: India, lit village by village. This is one of the best places on Earth to hear the difference between a city and a field: the pitch barely changes, but the brightness does.
